_comment: REVIEWER-ONLY authoring asset. Machine-readable cross-validation table for every Linux source reference the P3-M07 learner material makes. Verified against a real tree at exactly the pinned peeled commit. `line` is the 1-based line number of the FIRST match of `regex` in `file`, as reported by grep -n on that tree. Consumed by reviewer/run_m07_reviewer_check.sh with LINUX_SRC=<clone>. This file is not answer-bearing and is never readable from a learner path.

entries.topic: SVC entry point: EABI syscall dispatch
entries.note: Exact: ENTRY(vector_swi) is line 171.

entries.topic: ARM syscall table emission (EABI via calls-eabi.S)
entries.note: sys_call_table is also the operand of `adr tbl, sys_call_table` at line 235.

entries.regex: Pure EABI user space always put syscall number into scno \(r7\)
entries.topic: ARM EABI syscall-number register is r7
entries.note: Lies inside the CONFIG_AEABI branch; the surrounding region is 214-218.

entries.topic: The native syscall table body is pulled in from a GENERATED file
entries.note: CONFIG_AEABI selects <calls-eabi.S>; the #else branch at 359 pulls <calls-oabi.S>. Neither file is checked into the source tree: arch/arm/tools/Makefile:17 has Kbuild generate them into arch/arm/include/generated/ from arch/arm/tools/syscall.tbl. Teaching must say 'generated by Kbuild', not 'a file in arch/arm/kernel/'.

entries.topic: Emission of the sys_call_table symbol and its size
entries.note: The macro body emits `sym:` and `.size  \sym, . - \sym` (line 344), padding short tables with sys_ni_syscall.

entries.topic: Kbuild generates calls-eabi.S into arch/arm/include/generated/
entries.note: `gen := arch/$(ARCH)/include/generated` (line 9) and `syscall := $(src)/syscall.tbl` (line 13). This is why the EABI table body cannot be read in a pristine tree.

entries.topic: Fast syscall return path
entries.note: The label is emitted twice by design: the plain definition at line 40 and a tracing/context-tracking replacement at line 64. Line 40 is the one taken by the frozen non-tracing build.

entries.topic: Saved userspace register context restore
entries.note: Macro spans 293-329 (ENDPROC-adjacent); ARM-mode branch ends with `movs pc, lr`.

entries.regex: ^\s*movs\s+pc, lr\s+@ return & move spsr_svc into cpsr
entries.topic: Return-to-user: exception return moves SPSR into CPSR
entries.note: Emitted twice: ARM-mode variant at line 329 and Thumb2-mode variant at line 359. The frozen kernel is built in ARM mode, so line 329 is the effective one. Proves return-to-user is an exception return, not a normal branch.

entries.topic: Syscall dispatch macro (range check against NR_syscalls)
entries.note: Owned by entry-header.S, NOT entry-common.S.

entries.topic: r7 is the syscall-number register in the ARM kernel ABI
entries.note: Followed by tbl .req r8, why .req r8, tsk .req r9.

entries.topic: SWI vector slot resolves to vector_swi
entries.note: .L__vector_swi label is line 934 in section .stubs.

entries.topic: Vector table slot at offset +0x08 loads the SVC entry
entries.note: The vector table W() sequence (1084-1092) places vector_und at 0x04 and the SWI slot at 0x08.

entries.topic: Kernel image entry (M02 transfer point)
entries.note: Exact.

entries.topic: Boot-time identity/kernel page-table creation
entries.note: Call site `bl __create_page_tables` is line 139; ENDPROC at 377.

entries.topic: Boot-time MMU enable setup (TTBR0 write + DACR)
entries.note: ENDPROC at 490.

entries.topic: Point at which translation is actually enabled
entries.note: The SCTLR write `mcr p15, 0, r0, c1, c0, 0` is line 511, which is the M bit enable.

entries.topic: Post-MMU switch to virtual addressing
entries.note: Lives in head-common.S, NOT head.S. ENDPROC at 122, so the teaching region 77-122 is exact.

entries.topic: CONFIG_ARM_LPAE=y selects the 3-level (LPAE) header
entries.note: Unique in the file. The enclosing #ifdef CONFIG_ARM_LPAE is line 35, the #else line 37, and the 2-level include line 38; the block spans 35-39.

entries.topic: Exact non-LPAE header actually compiled under the frozen config
entries.note: Confirms the frozen config path resolves to pgtable-2level.h.

entries.regex: Hardware-wise, we have a two level page table structure
entries.topic: Hardware 2-level table vs Linux 3-level software abstraction
entries.note: Comment block starts at line 12.

entries.regex: be wrapped to fit a two level page table structure easily
entries.topic: Linux's three-level model is *wrapped* onto the hardware two-level layout
entries.note: Core evidence for the module's hardware-vs-software distinction.

entries.topic: Linux software PTE bit names (teaching vocabulary)
End of the L_PTE_* block
entries.note: Confirms the 119-127 range.

entries.topic: Device memory type encoding = 0b0100 << 2
entries.note: Real name is L_PTE_MT_DEV_SHARED (not DEV_SHARED).

entries.topic: Non-shared Device encoding = 0b1100 << 2
entries.note: Real name is L_PTE_MT_DEV_NONSHARED.

entries.topic: End of the MT nibble block
entries.note: Confirms the 165-176 range.

entries.topic: Section descriptor shareable bit (hardware-format vocabulary)
entries.note: PMD_SECT_* block runs 28-48.

entries.topic: Small-page descriptor XN bit position
entries.note: PTE_EXT_* block runs 69-81.

entries.topic: Access-permission field position in the hardware small-page descriptor
entries.note: AP encodings follow at 71-76.

entries.topic: PAGE_OFFSET is the configured kernel/user split point
entries.note: Under CONFIG_VMSPLIT_3G this resolves to 0xC0000000.

entries.topic: User address-space top: PAGE_OFFSET - 16M = 0xBF000000
entries.note: A KASAN variant follows at line 46; the frozen config has KASAN off, so line 44 is the effective definition. This is the source basis for teaching the user range as 0x00000000-0xBEFFFFFF.

entries.topic: The 16M below PAGE_OFFSET is module space, not user space
entries.note: Corroborates why the user top is TASK_SIZE and not PAGE_OFFSET.

entries.regex: we are not using split page tables
entries.topic: The frozen Cortex-A7 non-LPAE path does NOT use split page tables
entries.note: Line 36 is 'It is assumed that:'; line 37 is the assertion. This is the primary evidence for the module's TTBR correction.

entries.topic: Per-process address-space switch
entries.note: ENDs at 62.

entries.regex: ^\s*mcr\s+p15, 0, r1, c13, c0, 1\s+@ set context ID
entries.topic: Address-space switch sets CONTEXTIDR (ASID)
entries.note: Unconditional; the CONFIG_PID_IN_CONTEXTIDR block at 49-53 only folds the PID into r1.

entries.topic: Address-space switch writes TTBR0 only; no TTBR1 write
entries.note: Together with line 37 this refutes the oversimplified universal 'TTBR0=user / TTBR1=kernel' model.

entries.topic: Linux software PTE -> hardware short descriptor conversion
entries.note: ENDs at 109. This is where L_PTE_* and the MT nibble become hardware bits.

entries.topic: Primary Region Remap Register value used by the frozen kernel
entries.note: 0xff0a81a8 - the value the teaching fixtures assume.

entries.topic: Normal Memory Remap Register value used by the frozen kernel
entries.note: 0x40e040e0 - the value the teaching fixtures assume.

entries.topic: TTBR1 is programmed at boot by v7_ttb_setup, not on mm switch
entries.note: Part of the .macro v7_ttb_setup (line 146). The TTBCR write that consumes the `zero` argument is line 147 -- i.e. N=0 in the frozen path.

entries.topic: Boot-time TTBCR programming: N = 0, so TTBR0 spans the whole 4 GB
entries.note: Inside .macro v7_ttb_setup (line 146), invoked from __v7_setup at proc-v7.S:530 with r10 passed as the `zero` argument. This is the source basis for the module's TTBCR=0 claim, and it is why one TTBR0-resident table covers both the user and the kernel half.

entries.topic: Exact SCTLR bits the frozen Cortex-A7 non-LPAE path clears and sets
entries.note: Decisive for the descriptor-teaching assumption stamp. Bit arithmetic on mmuset=0x10c03c7d and clear=0x2120c302 gives TRE (bit 28) = 1 and AFE (bit 29) = 0 -- exactly what decode_short_desc.py, fixtures/descriptor_taught.json and the assessment starters assume. Note this symbol lives in proc-v7-2level.S (the non-LPAE variant actually compiled under CONFIG_ARM_LPAE=n), NOT in proc-v7.S. Contrast with the LPAE variant recorded separately: it leaves AFE set.

entries.topic: The LPAE variant of v7_crval keeps AFE set
entries.note: mmuset=0x30c03c7d sets bit 29 (AFE) and clear=0x0122c302 does not clear it, so the LPAE path runs with TRE=1, AFE=1. This is the contrast case that makes the non-LPAE constant diagnostic: an observed SCTLR with AFE=1 cannot come from the frozen non-LPAE path. Selected by proc-v7.S:23 (LPAE) vs :25 (non-LPAE).

entries.topic: Cortex-A7/A15-class processor setup entry
entries.note: Where PRRR/NMRR are actually programmed (lines 531-534 in the resume path, 178-181 in the setup path).

entries.regex: v7_ttb_setup r10, r4, r5, r8, r3\s+@ TTBCR, TTBRx setup
entries.topic: Boot-time TTBCR/TTBRx programming from __v7_setup
entries.note: Confirms TTBCR is programmed at boot with N=0 in this path.

entries.topic: Every new process pgd carries a copy of the kernel half
entries.note: Comment at 43-45: 'Copy over the kernel and IO PGD entries'. This is why one TTBR0-resident table can cover both halves.

entries.topic: ARM EABI __NR_getpid == 20
entries.note: Basis for Lab 7.2 moving 20 into r7 before svc #0. The .tbl column is the generic syscall number, which is the EABI numbering.

entries.topic: Official /proc/<pid> documentation section 1.1
entries.note: The maps entry is listed in Table 1-1 at line 140.

entries.regex: The /proc/PID/maps file contains the currently mapped memory regions
entries.topic: Authoritative maps line format (address, perms, offset, dev, inode, pathname)
entries.note: Learner-facing maps parsing must follow this, not a blog.

entries.topic: The authoritative /proc/PID/maps column header
entries.note: Preceded by 'The format is::' at line 384; worked example rows follow at 388-390. Learner-facing maps parsers must accept exactly this column set.

entries.topic: The +0x08 vector slot is a PC load through a relocated literal, not a branch
entries.note: Teaching precision: the SWI/SVC slot does NOT contain `b vector_swi`. Lines 1085 (ARM) and 1086 (THUMB) attach R_ARM_LDR_PC_G0 / R_ARM_THM_PC12 relocations against .L__vector_swi (line 934), and line 1087 is the relocated `ldr pc, .` instruction itself. The indirect load exists because the .stubs section can sit outside branch range. The instruction appears 3 times because the kernel emits three vector tables: .vectors (1081), .vectors.bhb.loop8 (1095, CONFIG_HARDEN_BRANCH_HISTORY) and .vectors.bhb.bpiall (1108).
